details: CONFIRMED by calling share() from the worktree's hook on the two replies above (0.50 and 0.42).
Runs are counted over WORD matches only, so commas, colons and full stops do not separate terms; an enumeration of
standard terms, which the new rule encourages, becomes one "English clause". The fixer's measure (143 replies of 24 Oct)
had one such list and it passed, but replies written under the new rule will carry more terms.
evidence: share("Что сделано: merge, branch, commit, fast-forward, hook теперь пишутся по-английски.", "CYRILLIC") -> 0.5
share("Готово: merge прошёл, CI green, review OK, paid eval run запущен, flaky test fixed.", "CYRILLIC") -> 0.4222
failing_case: Reply (owner language Russian): "Что сделано: merge, branch, commit, fast-forward, hook теперь пишутся по-английски."
share() = 0.50, under 0.60: the hook blocks and asks to rewrite in Russian. Same for
"Готово: merge прошёл, CI green, review OK, paid eval run запущен, flaky test fixed." (0.42).
The words list ignores punctuation, so "merge, branch, commit, fast-forward, hook" is one run of 5 Latin words (> TERM_RUN=3)
and counts in full. This is the brief's own case: a short Russian reply full of English IT terms, the very list the new rule names.
fix_hint: Split the text into segments at , ; : ( ) and similar before finding runs (a run never crosses punctuation), and let a
segment touch a native word across the punctuation (the nearest word before or after in the reply). A pure English reply
has no native word, so nothing is skipped. Add pass-case 1 and 4 to tests/test_it_terms.py.
pass_cases: 1. "Что сделано: merge, branch, commit, fast-forward, hook теперь пишутся по-английски." -> hook prints nothing.
2. TERMY of tests/test_it_terms.py -> hook prints nothing (works today).
3. ENGLISH and ENGLISH + " Готово." of tests/test_it_terms.py -> decision "block" (works today).
4. An English reply made of short sentences, "Done. Merged the branch. Gate is green. Paid run done. Next item starts now. Ok then." -> "block".
reason: tests/test_it_terms.py:52 (comma lists not refused) and :57 (short English sentences still refused) pass; :52 fails on the pre-fix hook.
findings.summary: a Russian reply that lists four or more English IT terms in a row (comma list) is still refused
